This has probably already been asked, has probably already been thrown around a lot, but sometimes it is good to throw around old ideas to find out where we are. I'm here to ask some stuff already said.

"Why are we not using bitcoin?" - Why should they want to use bitcoin when they already have a service? Paypal works well and they have no reason to see out of it. Getting one friend, one person to use bitcoin and showing them how it could be used as a means for currency.

All the benefits will not be the same for everyone but if you show them where it could be useful for them and then offer them as a market, they won't accept it immediately of course but they could. I personally have friends who are very interested in it but don't have an actual mean of being able to buy it. Widespread accessibility is bitcoins hardest obstacle so far, why don't we work on doing exactly that? Why don't we work on actual means of getting to the point. I'm not trying to imply that we haven't been so far, but we need to step up our game if we want to get to that point.

Just some food for thought.

tl;dr Where are we progressing and why should it be looked upon as a good thing? Discuss.

I'm not a big fan of forcing things. Most people shouldn't have bitcoin, because they can't secure it. Most people shouldn't invest in it, because it's too volatile and risky.
There are many ways of buying bitcoin, I think the exchange business is the most grown up in the entire industry.

There's 2 main reasons people adopt stuff. Because they are REALLY interested in it or because they have to. We are interested in it because we're nerds/libertarians/anarchists. You can talk to sex-workers all day about bitcoin, there'll be few who are interested enough to be able to buy some. When you take away all payment options except bitcoin for advertisement, suddenly they ARE able to do it.

Buenos Aires is one of the largest cities in the world when it comes to bitcoin adoption. Buenos Aires hasn't got a crazy bitcoin promo-team, they aren't the new silicon valley or the anarchistic capital of the world, people are just forced to use it if they want to interact financially with the rest of the world, or want to keep the value of their work.

L'Oreal can make a revolutionary champoo, and you can talk about it all day and I can find it fairly interesting, but I won't go out of my way into special stores to buy it. It's only when I get a rash from my normal shampoo I'll make the effort. (by figure of speech, I'm actually bald)

Point I'm trying to make is: let it all come naturally. People will find a way if they have to, and if there's business opportunities out there, entrepreneurs will grab them.

Realizing that we are forcing things is what we need to do, or at least one of the things that would help our cause. Give them reason within the reasons that they need to see, right? why don't we work on that. the people who may not be doing much can still be doing something if they are truly invested. Showing people and spreading the word helps but not forcing is the best thing to do. Show that we welcome them but don't want to ruin what they have, right?

Reason will be reason but some people will still not even need to accept, even though you believe that they do. you would have to show them that exact point, but not directly. That's what I think we don't understand, we have all this doubt clouding us on our future.

Also I like the point on the shampoo and Buenos Aires being the largest city that accepts it. They have a logical use and that's why they'll use it.
